scenarios.title: Kitchen grease fire spreading to cabinets

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! I was frying chicken at {location} and the pan caught on fire! It's starting to reach the cabinets!

options.text: Do not use water. Cover the pan with a metal lid or use baking soda if safe.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Smothering a grease fire removes oxygen. This is the safest immediate procedure.

options.text: Quickly throw a pitcher of water on the stove to put it out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water vaporizes instantly in hot grease, causing a violent explosion that spreads the fire.

options.text: Carefully grab the handle of the pan and carry it outside to the yard.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Carrying a burning pan usually results in spilling boiling, flaming grease on the carrier.

options.text: Turn off the heat source immediately if you can safely reach the stove knob.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Removing the heat source is a critical step in stopping a grease fire from escalating.

options.text: Open all the windows and exterior doors to let the toxic smoke out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening doors and windows creates drafts that feed oxygen to the fire, causing it to grow faster.

options.text: Try to beat the flames out with a wet dish towel or an apron.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Swatting at the fire can splash burning grease onto you and the surrounding cabinets.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Okay, I'm doing exactly what you said! But the fire already touched the ceiling, there's so much smoke!

options.text: Evacuate everyone immediately, close doors behind you if safe, and wait outside for the BFP.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Evacuation is safer than in-place suppression once the fire has spread.

options.text: Stay in the kitchen and keep trying to smother it with blankets until the BFP arrives.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: The fire has already spread beyond the pan.
options.explanation: Civilian suppression is dangerous once fire spreads to cabinets/ceiling.

options.text: Open the front door to push smoke out before evacuating.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ventilation feeds fire growth.

options.text: Run to your bedroom to grab your wallet and keys before exiting.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Re-entry risks entrapment and smoke inhalation.

options.text: Break the kitchen windows to let the smoke out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Breaking windows feeds the fire oxygen.

options.text: Hide in the bathroom and put a wet towel under the door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Bathrooms are not fire-rated safe rooms and become fatal smoke traps.

scenarios.title: Downed live wire sparking near residential gate

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: There's a loud buzzing noise!

options.text: 911, what is your exact location and emergency?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Standard protocol requires establishing location immediately.

options.text: Calm down, what's making the noise?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You must establish location before diagnosing the emergency.

options.text: Are you in danger right now?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Assessing immediate life threat is important, but location is still priority.

options.text: Please hold the line.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never place an active emergency on hold without knowing the location.

options.text: Is this a medical emergency?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Guessing the emergency wastes time. Ask directly.

options.text: BFP dispatcher, where is the fire?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Assuming it is a fire without asking can lead to incorrect dispatching.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I'm at {location}. A typhoon just blew through and a power line snapped. It's sparking on the wet pavement right in front of our gate!

options.text: Keep everyone inside, stay away from the gate, and do not step in any puddles.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Electricity can travel through wet ground (step potential).

options.text: Use a dry wooden broom to push the wire away from your gate.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Wood can contain moisture and conduct high-voltage electricity.

options.text: Slowly walk outside to see whose house it connects to.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Approaching a downed wire is a fatal electrocution risk.

options.text: Throw a heavy rubber mat over the wire to stop the sparks.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Household rubber is not rated for high-voltage utility lines.

options.text: Go turn off your main breaker switch immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The live wire is on the street side; touching your breaker won't stop the utility line.

options.text: Stay inside, I am dispatching the BFP to secure the area.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Securing the caller in place while deploying units is the correct action.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Understood, we are locking the doors and staying inside the house.

options.text: Maintain a perimeter from inside, do not attempt to leave until BFP and the power company arrive.
options.label: safe
options.hint: Isolation is critical around energized hazards.
options.explanation: Live-wire incidents require perimeter control and no civilian intervention.

options.text: Extinguish any small grass fires near the wire with a garden hose from your window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Spraying water near a live wire can conduct electricity back to the caller.

options.text: Evacuate the house immediately by jumping over the wire.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving near a live wire on wet ground is an electrocution hazard.

options.text: Tell your neighbors to come out and move their cars.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Drawing more people into the hazard zone increases casualty risk.

options.text: Wait for the sparks to stop, then carefully step around it to leave.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Downed lines can automatically re-energize without warning.

options.text: Throw buckets of sand onto the sparking wire from your porch.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing objects puts the caller in proximity to the electrical arc.

scenarios.title: E-bike lithium battery thermal runaway in living room

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My e-bike is smoking! I'm at {location} and the battery is hissing and shooting out white smoke!

options.text: Evacuate immediately. Do not try to move the bike or put it out.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Lithium-ion thermal runaway produces toxic gas and cannot be extinguished with household items.

options.text: Unplug it and drag the bike outside before it catches fire.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving a battery in thermal runaway exposes the caller to violent explosion and severe burns.

options.text: Throw a heavy blanket over the battery to smother the smoke.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lithium-ion batteries generate their own oxygen; a blanket will just catch fire.

options.text: Use your household fire extinguisher on the battery pack.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Standard ABC dry chemical extinguishers do not stop lithium-ion thermal runaway.

options.text: Pour buckets of water on it to cool it down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: While firefighters use water for cooling, a civilian cannot apply enough volume safely indoors.

options.text: Get out of the house now, the smoke is highly toxic.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Prioritizing life safety and toxic gas avoidance is the correct dispatch action.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Okay, I'm leaving the house now. It just started popping!

options.text: Wait outside at a safe distance and do not re-enter. The BFP is en route.
options.label: safe
options.hint: Thermal runaway requires professional HazMat/Fire response.
options.explanation: Lithium fires require massive amounts of water and specialized overhaul by the BFP.

options.text: Go back in quickly just to unplug the charger from the wall.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The toxic gases released can incapacitate a person in seconds.

options.text: Open all the windows from the outside to let the gas out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Approaching the structure exposes the caller to the highly toxic vapor cloud.

options.text: Try to spray a garden hose through the front door.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Not enough GPM to stop runaway.
options.explanation: A garden hose cannot cool the battery enough and puts the caller in the hazard zone.

options.text: Wait for it to stop popping, then go back inside to check the damage.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The environment remains toxic and the battery can reignite at any time.

options.text: Tell your neighbors to grab their extinguishers and help you.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Encouraging untrained civilians to fight a lithium fire will cause mass casualties.

scenarios.title: Home intrusion with caller hiding silently

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: (whispering) Please help... someone broke the glass downstairs. I'm hiding in my closet.

options.text: 911, can you safely whisper your address to me?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Verifying the location quietly ensures the PNP can be dispatched without exposing the caller.

options.text: SPEAK UP, I CANNOT HEAR YOU!
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Yelling at a hiding caller can cause them to make noise, alerting the intruder.

options.text: Where are you? Are you armed?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Getting location and assessing weapons is standard protocol.

options.text: Are they still inside? Go look.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never tell a hiding caller to leave concealment to investigate an intruder.

options.text: I will call you right back on video chat.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ringing the caller's phone or forcing video will expose their hiding spot.

options.text: Hold on, transferring you to the police.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Do not transfer a critical life-safety call without getting the address first.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: (whispering) I'm at {location}. I hear footsteps coming up the stairs.

options.text: Keep silent, dim your phone screen, turn off ringers, and stay on the line. PNP is on the way.
options.label: safe
options.hint: Stealth preserves caller safety until police entry.
options.explanation: Silent communication and concealment reduce detection risk during active intrusion.

options.text: Yell that the PNP is coming to scare them away.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Noise exposes the caller's location and escalates violence risk.

options.text: Grab a weapon and prepare to ambush them if they open the closet.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Dispatch guidance should prioritize survival and de-escalation.
options.explanation: Encouraging confrontation increases the risk of fatal outcomes.

options.text: Sneak out of the closet and try to run past them down the stairs.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Do not abandon a safe hiding spot.
options.explanation: Moving increases the chance of being spotted and intercepted by the intruder.

options.text: Turn on your phone flashlight so you can see them coming.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A light source in a dark room immediately gives away the caller's position.

options.text: Hang up the phone immediately so they don't hear you talking.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: An open line allows dispatch to hear what is happening and relay suspect movement to the PNP.

scenarios.title: Road rage incident with weapon brandishing

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: This crazy guy just cut me off and brake-checked me!

options.text: 911, what is your current location and direction of travel?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Establishing location and movement is required for PNP interception.

options.text: Did you hit his car?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Determine location before investigating the details of the incident.

options.text: Stop your car right now and wait for the police.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stopping in traffic with an aggressive driver makes the caller a sitting target.

options.text: Just ignore him and drive home.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Driving home can lead the aggressive driver to the caller's residence.

options.text: Follow him so you can get his license plate.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Following an aggressive driver escalates the road rage into a high-speed chase.

options.text: Where are you? Do you have his plate number?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Getting location and identifying information safely is correct.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I'm passing the mall at {location}. He just pulled up next to me and pointed a gun out the window!

options.text: Do not engage. Take the next turn to separate yourself, drive to the nearest PNP station, and stay on the line.
options.label: safe
options.hint: De-escalate and seek a safe haven.
options.explanation: Creating distance and driving to a police station deters the suspect and provides immediate safety.

options.text: Ram his car off the road before he shoots.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Do not escalate to deadly force with a vehicle.
options.explanation: Advising a civilian to intentionally crash their vehicle creates extreme liability and danger.

options.text: Roll down your window and tell him you are on the phone with 911.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Do not interact with the suspect.
options.explanation: Engaging the suspect can provoke them into firing the weapon.

options.text: Slam on your brakes and hide under the dashboard.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stopping the car makes the caller a stationary target and causes a traffic pileup.

options.text: Speed up and try to outrun him on the highway.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: High-speed driving increases the risk of a fatal multi-vehicle crash.

options.text: Pull over to the shoulder and put your hands up.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Do not surrender to a road rage suspect.
options.explanation: Pulling over gives the suspect total control over the situation.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Send the police! The security guard at {location} tackled a shoplifter and now they are fighting on the floor!

options.text: Are there any weapons involved?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Assessing for weapons dictates the severity of the PNP response.

options.text: Jump in and help the security guard!
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never instruct a civilian bystander to enter a physical altercation.

options.text: What did the shoplifter steal?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Property value is irrelevant when an active physical assault is occurring.

options.text: Tell the security guard to let him go.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dispatch cannot give tactical orders to private security via a bystander.

options.text: Is anyone injured and needing an ambulance?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Checking for injuries ensures MDRRMO is dispatched if needed.

options.text: Record it on your phone for evidence.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Recording distracts the caller from safety and providing updates.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: No weapons, but the shoplifter is punching the guard in the face repeatedly!

options.text: Keep your distance, ensure bystanders are clear, and I will rush PNP units to your location.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Bystander safety is paramount. PNP officers are trained to separate combatants.

options.text: Grab a heavy item from the store shelf and hit the shoplifter.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Civilian intervention can result in severe injury or legal liability.

options.text: Get close and yell that the police are coming.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Getting too close makes the caller a target for the violent suspect.

options.text: Block the exit doors so the shoplifter cannot escape.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Do not trap a violent suspect.
options.explanation: Blocking an exit forces a violent suspect to attack whoever is in the way.

options.text: Try to pull the shoplifter off the guard.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The caller lacks training and protective equipment to break up a fight.

options.text: Leave the store immediately and let them sort it out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: While distancing is good, leaving entirely means dispatch loses situational updates.

scenarios.title: Sudden cardiac arrest at the gym

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! A guy just collapsed off the treadmill at {location}!

options.text: Is he awake? Is he breathing normally?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Assessing consciousness and normal breathing determines if CPR is needed.

options.text: What is his name and age?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Gathering demographics wastes time during a potential cardiac arrest.

options.text: Put him in a chair so he can rest.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A collapsed patient should be left flat on the floor.

options.text: Did he hit his head?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Trauma assessment is good, but breathing takes priority.

options.text: Give him some water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never give liquids to an unconscious person; it causes choking/aspiration.

options.text: Check his pulse on his wrist.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Civilian pulse checks are unreliable. Focus on breathing.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: He's not responding! He's just making weird gasping sounds!

options.text: That is agonal breathing, not normal breathing. Start chest compressions immediately; push hard and fast in the center of the chest. MDRRMO is en route.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Gasping in an unresponsive patient indicates cardiac arrest. Immediate CPR and AED use are required.

options.text: He is breathing. Just roll him on his side and wait for the ambulance.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Mistaking agonal gasps for breathing delays life-saving CPR.

options.text: Do mouth-to-mouth rescue breaths first.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Modern dispatcher-assisted CPR prioritizes hands-only chest compressions.

options.text: Slap his face and yell his name to wake him up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Physical stimulation wastes time when compressions are needed.

options.text: Check his pockets for heart medication.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Medications cannot restart a stopped heart; only CPR and an AED can.

options.text: Wait for the MDRRMO medics to arrive before touching him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Delaying CPR until medics arrive drastically reduces survival chances.

scenarios.title: Severe boiling water burn in kitchen

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: My grandmother accidentally pulled a pot of boiling water off the stove at {location}! Her chest and arms are burned!

options.text: Is she having any trouble breathing?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Burns to the chest/neck can cause airway swelling. Always check airway first.

options.text: Apply butter or oil to the burns immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Grease traps heat and causes infection. Never apply butter to a burn.

options.text: Pop the blisters so the fluid can drain.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Popping blisters opens the skin to severe infection.

options.text: Put ice packs directly on her skin.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Direct ice causes frostbite and tissue damage to compromised skin.

options.text: Is she still wearing the hot, wet clothing?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Hot wet clothing continues to burn the skin and must be removed safely.

options.text: Tell her to walk to the shower.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A severely burned elderly patient may go into shock and fall.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: She's breathing fine but crying in pain. Her shirt is soaked with hot water!

options.text: Carefully remove the wet shirt. Cool the burns with cool running water for 10-20 minutes. MDRRMO is on the way.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Removing the heat source (wet clothes) and using cool (not ice) water halts tissue damage.

options.text: Leave the shirt on and wrap her in a thick blanket.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: The shirt is still boiling hot.
options.explanation: Keeping hot clothing on the skin worsens the burn depth.

options.text: Peel the shirt off, even if it is stuck to the skin.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If clothing is melted or stuck, peeling it rips the skin off. Cut around it instead.

options.text: Apply toothpaste to the burns to cool them down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Toothpaste is unsterile and must be scrubbed out by doctors later, causing agony.

options.text: Have her drink a large glass of ice water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Major burn patients should not eat or drink due to surgery requirements and shock.

options.text: Put a tight bandage over her chest.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Tight bandages restrict breathing and circulation as the burn swells.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! We are at the park at {location}. My son got stung by a bee and his face is swelling up!

options.text: Is he having difficulty breathing or wheezing?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Airway compromise is the primary life threat in anaphylaxis.

options.text: Try to suck the venom out of the sting.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sucking venom is ineffective and introduces mouth bacteria.

options.text: Put mud on the sting to soothe it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Mud causes infection and does not stop an allergic reaction.

options.text: Does he have a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen)?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Identifying if life-saving medication is available is critical.

options.text: Have him run around to keep his heart rate up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Exertion accelerates the spread of venom and worsens shock.

options.text: Give him a sip of water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: With a swelling airway, liquids pose a severe choking hazard.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: He's wheezing really bad! I have his EpiPen right here in my bag!

options.text: Administer the EpiPen into his outer thigh immediately. Lay him flat and raise his legs. MDRRMO is responding.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Immediate epinephrine and the shock position (legs elevated) save lives during anaphylaxis.

options.text: Wait to see if the wheezing stops before using the EpiPen.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Delaying epinephrine administration is the leading cause of death in anaphylaxis.

options.text: Inject the EpiPen into his chest.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: EpiPens are designed for intramuscular injection in the thick vastus lateralis (outer thigh) muscle.

options.text: Give him an antihistamine pill instead.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Oral antihistamines take 30-60 minutes to work and do not reverse airway swelling.

options.text: Sit him straight up and tilt his head back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sitting a patient in anaphylactic shock upright can cause cardiac arrest due to sudden blood pressure drop (empty vena cava syndrome).

options.text: Use the EpiPen on the bee sting directly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The medication must go into the large thigh muscle to circulate systemically, not locally at the sting.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Oh my god, my neighbor's apartment is on fire! There's smoke pouring out of Unit 4B and I can see flames! The fire alarms are going off everywhere!

options.text: Advise caller to evacuate the building immediately via the nearest safe exit and not use elevators.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Prioritizing the caller's immediate safety by instructing evacuation from a burning building is crucial. Elevators can fail or become smoke traps in a fire.

options.text: Instruct caller to try and knock on Unit 4B's door to see if anyone is inside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Approaching a burning unit is extremely dangerous due to heat, smoke, and potential structural collapse, putting the caller at severe risk.

options.text: Tell caller to grab a fire extinguisher and try to put out the fire in Unit 4B themselves.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A fire already producing visible flames and thick smoke is beyond the scope of a portable extinguisher and too dangerous for an untrained individual to tackle.

options.text: Ask caller to check other floors for fire spread before evacuating.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The caller's priority should be their own immediate evacuation. Checking other floors can delay their escape and expose them to further danger.

options.text: Tell caller to find the building manager to report the fire before calling emergency services.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Emergency services (911/BFP) are already on the line and are the primary responders for a building fire, not building management for initial reporting.

options.text: Keep the caller on the line and ask for a detailed description of the smoke color and flame intensity.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: While information is useful, the caller is in immediate danger. Immediate evacuation instructions are paramount over detailed descriptive questioning at this point.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: It's the Grandview Apartments, 123 Main Street! I saw Mrs. Rodriguez earlier, but I don't see her now. The smoke is getting thicker in the hallway!

options.text: Dispatch a BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) fire_truck with lights and sirens, advising all residents to evacuate and check for trapped individuals.
options.label: safe
options.hint: Immediate, high-priority dispatch with safety instructions.
options.explanation: This is the correct, urgent response for a confirmed apartment building fire, prioritizing rapid intervention, resident evacuation, and potential rescue operations.

options.text: Dispatch a BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) fire_truck to the scene, but advise them to wait for the police department to secure the area first.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Delaying fire response for police when a confirmed fire is spreading in a residential building with potential entrapment is inappropriate and could lead to severe consequences.

options.text: Advise the caller that building management should handle this and provide them with the building management contact information.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: An active fire with visible flames and thick smoke is a severe emergency requiring BFP intervention, not just building management.

options.text: Dispatch a BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) fire_truck without lights and sirens to avoid panic among residents.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lights and sirens are crucial for rapid response, ensuring clear passage for emergency vehicles and alerting the public to the imminent danger, which outweighs concerns about panic in a real fire.

options.text: Instruct the caller to try and locate a fire alarm pull station if they haven't heard alarms on their floor.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The caller explicitly stated that fire alarms are 'going off everywhere,' indicating the system is active. Their priority should be safe evacuation, not additional alarm activation.

options.text: Request a non-emergency police unit to assess the situation before sending fire services, in case it's a false alarm.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The caller describes visible flames and thick smoke, which are clear indicators of a confirmed, severe fire, not a false alarm. This would lead to a dangerous delay.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I'm a security guard at Apex Logistics Warehouse, and there's a huge fire inside! I just finished my rounds, came back to the main office, and the alarms are blaring, smoke is everywhere near the back loading docks!

options.text: Advise the caller to evacuate to a safe distance immediately and await BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) arrival, providing details from afar.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Given the size of the fire and unknown contents, the caller's immediate safety by evacuating to a safe distance is the top priority.

options.text: Instruct the caller to try and locate the fire's source to determine what's burning.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Entering a large, smoky warehouse with unknown contents, potentially hazardous, is extremely dangerous and could lead to the caller being overcome by smoke or fire.

options.text: Tell the caller to try and activate the sprinkler system manually if it hasn't started yet.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Manual activation could expose the caller to significant danger. The system might already be compromised or active, and this is not a task for a non-firefighter in an active blaze.

options.text: Ask the caller to check employee muster points to see if all staff have evacuated.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: While knowing if staff are safe is important, the caller's personal safety is paramount. BFP personnel will manage evacuation verification upon arrival.

options.text: Suggest the caller use a forklift to move any flammable materials away from the fire.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Attempting to operate heavy machinery in a smoke-filled, burning warehouse is incredibly dangerous and could exacerbate the situation or injure the caller.

options.text: Inquire if the caller has access to the building's schematics to identify storage areas.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: While useful information, delaying immediate safety instructions or dispatch for this information is not ideal. BFP will request this upon arrival if needed.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: It's 456 Industrial Parkway. I think there are mostly electronics and some solvents back there, but I'm not sure specifically. I don't think anyone else is inside, everyone cleared out after the alarm, but it's a big place.

options.text: Dispatch a BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) fire_truck with full lights and sirens, alerting them to potential hazardous materials and requesting a HazMat team for assessment.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: This is the comprehensive and appropriate response for a commercial warehouse fire, especially with unknown potentially hazardous contents, ensuring rapid, specialized intervention.

options.text: Dispatch a BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) fire_truck without sirens, as it's a commercial area and shouldn't cause panic.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sirens are critical for emergency vehicles to clear traffic and respond rapidly, especially to a high-severity incident like a commercial fire, where speed can prevent greater damage or loss of life.

options.text: Advise the caller to monitor the fire from a safe distance and call back if it appears to be spreading outside the building.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Delays intervention for an active fire.
options.explanation: The fire is already confirmed and internal, requiring immediate BFP response, not just monitoring. Waiting for external spread will only worsen the situation.

options.text: Instruct the caller to find a main water valve to try and shut off water to the building to prevent further damage.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Can you go into the attic to see if you can locate the source of the fire?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Directing the caller into an attic with a suspected electrical fire is extremely dangerous due to potential collapse, electrocution, smoke inhalation, and rapid fire spread.

options.text: Could you try to pour water onto the warm ceiling area to cool it down?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pouring water onto an electrical fire from below is extremely dangerous, risks electrocution, and can cause ceiling collapse and water damage without effectively suppressing the fire.

options.text: Have you called an electrician to come take a look at it first?
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: An active fire, especially one with a burning smell and warm ceiling, requires immediate BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) response, not an electrician, who is not equipped for fire suppression.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: It's 789 Maple Drive, and there are three of us. No smoke detectors are going off yet, but the smell is getting stronger. I'll go turn off the main breaker right now!

options.text: I am sending help. (Bureau of Fire Protection) for a 'Residential Structure Fire - Electrical' priority and I advise you to immediate evacuation of all occupants, instructing them to stay outside and away from the house.
options.label: safe
options.hint: This response ensures immediate BFP arrival for a serious residential fire and prioritizes the safety of all occupants by getting them clear of the hazard.
options.explanation: Immediately dispatching BFP for a residential attic fire with electrical involvement is crucial due to the hidden nature of the fire and potential for rapid spread and collapse; evacuation ensures occupant safety.

options.text: Tell the caller to go into the attic to try and locate the exact wiring issue.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Entering an attic with an active electrical fire is extremely dangerous due to smoke, heat, electrocution risk, and potential for structural collapse.
options.explanation: Instructing the caller to enter an attic with an active electrical fire is extremely dangerous due to the risks of electrocution, smoke inhalation, structural collapse, and rapid fire spread.

options.text: Suggest opening windows and doors to try and air out the smoke from the house.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Opening windows can provide oxygen to the hidden fire, potentially accelerating its growth and spread.
options.explanation: Opening windows and doors can introduce oxygen to a hidden fire, potentially fueling its growth and accelerating its spread, making the situation worse.

options.text: Advise the caller to try and remove any valuable items from the attic before BFP arrives.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Attempting to retrieve items from an attic fire risks severe injury or death; lives are prioritized over property.
options.explanation: Prioritizing property retrieval over personal safety in an attic fire is extremely dangerous, as the structure could collapse or the fire could intensify rapidly, trapping the caller.

options.text: Instruct the caller to remain inside the house to await BFP, as it is safest there.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: Remaining inside a house with an active fire, especially one originating in the attic, is extremely dangerous.
options.explanation: Remaining inside a house with an active fire, particularly one in the attic, is highly dangerous due to smoke inhalation, potential for collapse, and rapid fire spread.

options.text: Tell the caller to just monitor the situation and call back if it gets worse.
options.label: unsafe
options.hint: An active fire, especially a hidden one, requires immediate BFP response; waiting will only allow it to escalate.
options.explanation: An active fire with smoke and crackling in an attic requires immediate BFP (Bureau of Fire Protection) intervention; 'monitoring' allows the fire to escalate, endangering lives and property.
